_why: Module-level layer map for sms_tool. Numbering follows docs/architecture.md: layer 1 is the outermost surface, layer 5 the innermost adapter. Imports point inward, so an edge may go from a lower layer to a higher one, never the reverse. A module no rule claims fails the check, so the map cannot silently lose coverage. Enforced by scripts/import_layer_ratchet.py.

layers.1: surface (IPC envelope, operator output, stdout mirror, WPF-facing reads)
layers.2: command adapter (cli, cli_parsers, commands, doctor, diagnostics)
layers.3: application workflow (registration, payment, mailbox, accounts, auth)
layers.4: adapter (providers, store, payment lanes, drivers, browser, phone, wallet)
layers.5: foundation & domain contract (kernel, config, geo, proxy, models, shared seams)

sms_tool.paypal -> sms_tool.paypal.orche.reason: the paypal package __init__ re-exports its own browser-lane orchestrator; a package facade is the documented import surface (ADR-0009)

sms_tool.registration_drivers.playwright.reason: the playwright driver shell drives the browser_flow workflow; the shell is a registration_drivers member, so the package layer is one below the flow it owns

sms_tool.payment.qualification_batch ->.reason: 支付资格 batch (2026-10-26): the whole-batch circuit breaker is a leaf policy object shared by the registration batch and promotion_batch; a payment-lane batch runner needs the same guard, and the shared-batch-policy keys live on that object. Inverting the call would mean every caller passing a breaker factory into the batch.
